title: Your Insecure MCP Server Won't Survive Production — Tun Shwe, Lenses
talk_summary: A talk on designing and securing MCP servers for production, arguing that good interface design (fewer, coarser tools; constrained schemas; minimal responses) and good security are the same discipline. It then walks through OAuth 2.1 flows (DCR vs CIMD, PKCE, token exchange) and enterprise layers like per-tool RBAC, data masking, and end-to-end tracing.

takeaways.technique: Coarse-grained outcome tools instead of fine-grained API wrappers
takeaways.what_they_do: Collapse many fine-grained operations into a single tool that produces a desired outcome, so there is one permission check, one audit log entry, and one place to enforce authorization.
takeaways.evidence_quote: squash all the fine-grained operations or underlying API calls into a single coarse-grained operation that produces a desired outcome

takeaways.technique: Return only what the agent needs (strip tool payloads)
takeaways.what_they_do: Tool responses are trimmed to the minimum fields needed for the immediate task; PII, internal IDs, credentials, and system details are stripped before they enter the context window.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If the agent doesn't need a piece of data for its immediate task, then don't return it.

takeaways.technique: Schema-level input constraints (enums, flat dicts, Pydantic)
takeaways.what_they_do: Accept only top-level primitives/enums and non-nested dicts; reject free-form nested payloads because unconstrained string args passed downstream are the root of injection flaws.
takeaways.evidence_quote: reject free-form nested payloads to avoid command injection flaws where the root cause is almost always unconstrained string arguments

takeaways.what_they_do: Scope permissions at the tool and resource level rather than the session level, and mark non-destructive tools read-only so clients can enforce boundaries; read-only tools can become resources.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Scope permissions at the tool and resource level, not the session level.

takeaways.technique: End-to-end tracing of agent tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Log which agent called which tool, with what parameters, and what data was returned, and trace the full request from validation through execution to response.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you cannot trace what an agent did end to end, you cannot govern it.

takeaways.technique: Data masking before the agent sees PII
takeaways.what_they_do: Mask PII fields (email, phone, national insurance numbers) before they reach the agent, since agents should not handle data they have no business with.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents should never be exposed to data that they have no business handling
